title: Data Sources & Ingestion
html:
Everything downstream depends on how you move data into Data 360. This phase covers the ingestion channels, how a data stream becomes a Data Lake Object (DLO), refresh schedules, connectors, and the error/observability patterns you must know for the exam and for real implementations.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Choose the correct ingestion mechanism for a requirement: CRM connector, Ingestion API, batch loader, streaming, or cloud-storage connector.
  • Explain how a data stream produces a DLO and what "lz-append" vs "upsert" DLO types mean.
  • Configure source objects/fields and refresh schedules at the right grain.
  • Troubleshoot common ingestion failures (schema mismatch, primary-key issues, mapping errors).
  • Mirror the ingestion patterns in DataCloudIngestionService and Data_Stream_Log__c.

1. Ingestion Channels

Data 360 intentionally offers multiple ways in. Pick the one that matches the source, latency, and volume.

ChannelWhen to useLatencyNotes
Salesforce CRM connectorSalesforce objects (Contact, Account, Case, Opportunity, custom objects)near-real-time scheduledSimplest; a stream per object/Subject Area; creates DLOs per object.
Marketing Cloud connectorMarketing Cloud data extensions/sendsbatch / scheduledBrings engagement data (opens, clicks, sends) into the profile.
Ingestion API (/services/data/vXX/ingest/...)Custom/streaming sources, web/mobile eventsnear-real-timePush JSON payloads; low-latency; supports high throughput.
Batch loaderLarge historical files (CSV/JSON/Parquet) via SFTP/URLbatchOne-time or scheduled bulk loads from SFTP, Amazon S3, Azure, GCS, etc.
Cloud-storage connectorsS3 / Azure Blob / GCS object storesbatch / incrementalNative connectors + Zero-Copy options.
MuleSoft / ETLComplex source landscapesdependsMuleSoft ingestion accelerators, Informatica, etc. feed the Ingestion API or batch.

Real-time vs. batch (an exam favourite)

  • Batch is for historical/volume loads and re-runs; freshness depends on the refresh schedule.
  • Streaming (Ingestion API) is for events that must act immediately: web session, cart abandoned, service chat, POS live.
  • A streaming case becomes real in every layer: real-time calculated insights, real-time segments, real-time data actions, and Data Graphs for Agentforce almost always start from streaming ingestion.

2. Data Streams and DLOs

A data stream is the configured pipeline for one source→target pair. Configuring a stream requires:

  1. Connector + source — choose the source (CRM object, batch file, API app).
  2. Subject Area — the business topic (e.g. Sale, Customer, WebActivity).
  3. DLO output — the raw object the stream creates, named by convention <Area> with a _dlm suffix (data lake model), e.g. POS_Sale__dlm.

  4. DLO type — how the raw store is written:

    • lz-append (raw landing zone) — append-only, no dedupe; good for event/historical payloads; every load appends rows.
    • upsert — upsert by external key; keeps the latest version of each record; good for master data like customer.
  5. Schema — the source schema is captured; you then map fields downstream when building the DMO (Phase 3).
  6. Refresh schedule — manual, interval, or schedule (minutes→daily) for batch; streaming is continuous.

Primary keys and dedupe

Solidizing identity begins here: selecting the primary key for a stream determines how upsert DLOs stay unique and how hard the mapping phase has to work. Best practice is a stable external key from the source (e.g. customer_id, order_number). If a source lacks one, you may need to compose one (store_id + local_order_id) — this is a classic exam scenario.

3. Configuring a CRM Connector Stream (walkthrough)

  1. In the Data 360 tab (Setup), go to Connectors & Streams → Data Sources and enable the Salesforce CRM connector.
  2. Create a new Data Source for the object family (e.g. Sales). Pick the Salesforce org.
  3. Add a Stream per object that matters (e.g. Opportunity, Contact). Choose the DLO type (default lz-append) and, for master data, switch to upsert keyed on the record's external id.
  4. Select which fields to ingest (fewer fields = less DWU/DTO consumption and simpler mappings).
  5. Set the refresh schedule (e.g. every 30 minutes) and decide whether to backfill (initial load of history).
  6. Monitor the Ingestion Jobs table; on failure the stream shows job errors with the offending row/field.
DTO / DWU note: Data 360 consumes entitlements — Data Transform Objects (DTO) and Data Warehouse Units (DWU) are consumed by mapping/query workloads. Consultants must size fields consumed and query fresh data thoughtfully; the exam tests this resource-consciousness, not the tariff numbers.

4. Ingestion API and Streaming Detail

The Ingestion API receives JSON payloads. A realistic payload for a service-event stream:

json
{
  "data": {
    "type": "data",
    "attributes": {
      "source": "chat-sdk",
      "objects": [
        {
          "external_id": "ch_000123",
          "customer_id": "cus_9876",
          "event": "chat_started",
          "sentiment": "negative",
          "timestamp": "2026-01-07T09:14:32Z"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

After a successful push, each payload object becomes a row in the stream's DLO; invalid rows (wrong types, missing keys) are dropped into the ingestion error log you review in Data 360, not silently accepted.

Programmatic access from Apex (lab mirror)

Real Data 360 configuration cannot be deployed by sf, so this repo shows the client-side pattern: DataCloudIngestionService builds and validates a JSON payload, checks source/grain constraints, upserts a Data_Stream_Log__c header + rows, and (optionally) publishes a Data_Action_Event__e platform event — the same shape a callout to /services/data/v68.0/ingest/<stream/> would take. Verbatim pattern from the lab:

apex
// Build the payload one record at a time, then send ONE logical batch.
for (SObject rec : records) {
    payload += '{ "external_id": "' + esc((String)rec.get('External_Key__c')) + '",'
               + ' "customer_id": "' + esc((String)rec.get('Customer_Key__c')) + '" }';
}

The service then persists the DML batch + event publish (bulk, one call each) and records outcome for observability.

5. Observability and Troubleshooting

The consultant's most common real-world task is diagnosing a "stream failed" alert. Keep this checklist in your head:

SymptomLikely causeCheck
Job shows Failed with schema errorField type mismatch between source and DLOIngestion Jobs → row/field error message
Rows "missing" but job says successPayload rows dropped as invalid; mapping excluded themError log / "invalid records" tab
Stream hung "Running"Large backfill + oversubscribed DWUPause/rerun; reduce scheduled concurrency
Duplicated unified profiles laterWeak primary key on an append DLORe-ingest as upsert keyed on external id
401s on Ingestion APIAuth/bearer token scope (Data 360 perm set)Service App / permission-set assignment

Also: refresh schedules vs. activation schedules are different settings. A stream can refresh hourly while a Marketing activation publishes daily or real-time; misreading "how fresh is this audience?" is a frequent exam trap.

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: Stream-planning table

From the "Global Support Center"-style scenario (Phase 17), fill a table with: source system → channel (connector/API/batch/streaming) → DLO name → DLO type (append/upsert/pk) → refresh schedule → data space. Plan for four sources: CRM cases, web chat events, a warehouse orders dump, and loyalty points.

Exercise 2: Ingestion payload

Using scripts/apex/ingest_payload.apex, build a 3-record JSON payload for chat_events with external_id, customer_id, event, sentiment. Validate there are no duplicate external_ids and no missing keys before "sending" (the lab's DataCloudIngestionService.validatePayload does this in memory).

Exercise 3: Failure drill

Given: an upsert stream keyed on external_id, and a new source file in which 2 rows carry duplicate external_id. Predict: (a) what the DLO shows, (b) how to fix it, (c) what the downstream mapping must enforce. Then implement the dedupe check in the service test (DataCloudIngestionServiceTest).

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
Data sourceA connected system (CRM, MC, storage, API) that feeds Data 360.
Data streamA configured ingestion pipeline from one source to one DLO.
DLOData Lake Object: the raw data object written by a stream.
lz-appendAppend-only DLO type storing every ingested row (raw landing zone).
upsert DLODLO type that updates/inserts rows by a primary/external key.
Ingestion APIREST API for pushing low-latency JSON event data into a stream's DLO.
Refresh scheduleHow often a batch stream re-pulls source data.
Zero-copyReading data in external lakes/stores without copying it into Data 360.
DTO/DWUData Transform Objects / Data Warehouse Units: metered resources consumed by mapping and query workloads.

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can match a source+latency+volume to the correct ingestion channel.
  • I can explain how a stream creates a DLO and why DLO type (append vs upsert) matters.
  • I can select a primary key (or compose one) for an upsert stream.
  • I can distinguish refresh schedules from activation schedules.
  • I can trace an ingestion error to its remedy using the job/error UIs.
  • I can read and extend DataCloudIngestionService and its test class.
